**Section D: Composition (10 marks).** Write a composition of between 200-250 words on ONE of the topics below.

**Topic 1.** Your parents want you to become a medical doctor after you leave school but this is not a profession you like. Write a letter to your uncle pleading to him to convince your parents to accept your choice of becoming a journalist. You may want to give the reasons for your choice, the importance of this job to the family or society, the opportunities that may come with time etc. Your name is Gota and your address is Post Office Box 34, Figa. Your uncle is called Kasa.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC série A évalue à la fois le respect du format imposé (lettre personnelle, discours, composition narrative) et la qualité du contenu. Le sujet proposant un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun des trois sujets proposés, avec une longueur adaptée à la consigne (200-250 mots).

## Topic 1 - Personal letter (modèle, environ 230 mots)

Gota
P.O. Box 34, Figa

Dear Uncle Kasa,

I hope you are doing well. I am writing to ask for your help with something that has been troubling me for a while: my parents want me to become a medical doctor after I leave school, but this is not a career I feel drawn to. What I truly want to do is become a journalist.

I know medicine is a respected and stable profession, and I understand why my parents wish this path for me. But I believe journalism suits my strengths far better: I love writing, asking questions, and telling stories that matter to people. A good journalist can inform citizens, hold leaders accountable, and give a voice to communities that are rarely heard — this, to me, feels every bit as valuable to our society as practising medicine.

I also believe journalism offers real opportunities today, from television and radio to the growing world of digital and online media, both within Cameroon and internationally. With time and experience, a career in journalism could open doors just as rewarding as those in medicine, while allowing me to do work I am genuinely passionate about.

Uncle, I am asking for your help because I know my parents respect your opinion greatly. Could you please speak with them on my behalf, and help them see that choosing journalism does not mean choosing failure, but simply choosing a different way to contribute meaningfully to our society?

Thank you for considering this. I look forward to hearing from you.

Your nephew,
Gota

**Section D: Composition (10 marks).** Write a composition of between 200-250 words on ONE of the topics below.

**Topic 2.** The Secretary of State for Secondary Education is visiting your school. Among some of the worries you have is the alarming rate of drug consumption among your schoolmates. As the senior prefect of your school, write a speech that you will present during this occasion. In your speech, give some of the reasons for this phenomenon, the consequences, what the school has been doing to stop it, and what you expect the Secretary of State to do to help the situation. Your name is Kika and the name of your school is GBHS Tana.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Speech (modèle, environ 260 mots)

Honourable Secretary of State, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

As Senior Prefect of GBHS Tana, I welcome this opportunity to raise a concern that troubles many of us on this campus: the alarming rate of drug consumption among our schoolmates.

In recent years, we have noticed a worrying number of students turning to substances such as tramadol, alcohol and, in some cases, harder drugs. Several factors explain this trend: peer pressure, the desire to appear "grown up," stress linked to academic performance, and, for some, difficult circumstances at home that leave them searching for an escape.

The consequences are serious. Affected students often show declining academic performance, increased absenteeism, and behavioural problems that disrupt classroom learning for everyone. In more severe cases, we have seen promising students drop out entirely, their futures placed at real risk.

Our school has not remained passive. The administration has introduced sensitisation talks during assemblies, strengthened collaboration with parents when warning signs appear, and works closely with school counsellors to support affected students rather than simply punishing them.

However, we believe more can be done at a higher level. We respectfully ask the Ministry to consider stronger control over the sale of certain medications to minors, and to support more school counselling programmes across the country, not only in urban centres.

Honourable Secretary of State, our generation's future depends on how seriously this problem is addressed today. We count on your support.

Thank you.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section D: Composition (10 marks).** Write a composition of between 200-250 words on ONE of the topics below.

**Topic 3.** Your friend invited you for his birthday party last week. The party was very interesting and you enjoyed yourself very well. Write a composition in which you say when, where, and what happened there. Also say what particularly attracted your attention. Your friend's name is Bah.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Composition (modèle, environ 220 mots)

Last Saturday, I attended the birthday party of my friend Bah, and it turned out to be one of the most enjoyable evenings I have had in a long time.

The party took place at Bah's family compound, which had been beautifully decorated with colourful balloons and string lights for the occasion. When I arrived at around 5 p.m., music was already playing and several of our classmates had gathered, chatting and laughing near the entrance.

Throughout the evening, we played games, danced to popular songs, and, of course, enjoyed a delicious spread of food, from grilled chicken to jollof rice and a large birthday cake that Bah cut amid cheers from all of us. What particularly attracted my attention was a short speech Bah's older brother gave, sharing funny childhood stories about Bah that none of us had heard before — it had the entire room laughing until our stomachs hurt.

As the evening went on, a few of us also helped organise a small dance competition, which added even more energy to the celebration. By the time I left, well after dark, I felt genuinely grateful to have been part of such a warm and lively gathering.

That evening reminded me how simple moments, shared with good friends, can become some of our happiest memories.

### Piège à éviter
Dans une composition narrative comme le sujet 3, l'erreur fréquente est de rester dans une simple liste chronologique d'événements sans jamais préciser ce qui a "particulièrement attiré l'attention" du narrateur, alors que la consigne l'exige explicitement.

### Conseil
Quelle que soit la consigne narrative, relis-la une dernière fois avant de conclure ta rédaction pour vérifier que chaque élément explicitement demandé (ici : quand, où, ce qui s'est passé, ce qui a attiré l'attention) apparaît clairement dans le texte.
